target: A warehouse staging cell must handle every arrival trace satisfying the deterministic envelope alpha(t)=120+30t orders over any interval of length t. Its guaranteed processing service is beta(t)=50*max(t-2,0) orders. The team needs worst-case deterministic bounds for required staging-buffer capacity and order delay; average utilization alone is not an acceptable guarantee.
surface: A previous warehouse plan compared average rates only: arrivals averaged 30 orders per time unit and processing capacity was 50, so it reported 40% spare throughput and provisioned no explicit burst buffer or deterministic delay allowance.
structural: A packet network bounded a token-bucket arrival curve alpha(t)=sigma+r*t through a rate-latency service curve beta(t)=R*max(t-T,0), with r<R. Network calculus gave worst-case backlog as the maximum vertical deviation, sigma+r*T, and worst-case delay as the maximum horizontal deviation, T+sigma/R.
rubric: Explicitly selects deterministic network-calculus vertical and horizontal deviations.
Maps sigma=120, r=30, R=50, and T=2 and checks r<R.
Computes worst-case delay as 2+120/50=4.4 time units.
States that bounds depend on all traces respecting the arrival envelope and the service guarantee, rather than only average rates.
